messages:
mike: Noticed something odd: p99 for latencies in eu-central is lower than us-east for the same endpoint. p50/p95 look normal. anyone else?

jess: that sounds backwards. region compare query or dashboard rollup?

mike: dashboard rollup widget (region breakdown). I ran the raw query per-host and p99 matches expectations there.

rachel: could be an aggregation/compression artifact. we've seen tdigest compression cause quantile inversion on sparse tails before. what rollup backend are you using?

mike: rollup uses aggregated tdigest buckets in the metric-store. I remember we lowered compression to save memory last month.

own: that'd do it. low compression -> coarse t-digest -> bad p99 especially when sample_count is small or skewed. Do we have sample_count for those regions?

mike: the widget doesn't show counts. when I ran `SELECT count(*) FROM rollup WHERE region='eu-central' AND window=5m` I saw ~120 samples. us-east had 4k.

ux-lina: UX note: showing p50/p95/p99 without sample_count or percentile method invites confusion. can we show a tiny tooltip: "method: t-digest (compression=100), samples=120"?

jess: +1. Also we should mark p99 as unreliable if sample_count < 500 and compression < 200. quick heuristic.

own: ops: any recent change to tdigest compression param?

infra-bot: config change: metrics/tdigest.compression reduced from 200 -> 80 at 7765400000 (by infra-auto-scaler).

rachel: there's the smoking gun. compression=80 will underrepresent the extreme tail. we should revert for global rollups or at least per-quantile risk-tier.

mike: why did auto-scaler touch that? was it a memory pressure mitigation?

infra-bot: alert: autoscale memory pressure triggered a global small-tweak job at 7765399000 to lower tdigest default compression.

jess: proposal: 1) revert compression to 200 for quantiles p95+ on rollups, 2) add sample_count badge to the dashboard, 3) add an "unreliable" flag when conditions met, 4) make rollup compute exact percentile for sample_count<1000 via offline merge for high-precision.

own: pragmatic: revert now for prod rollups then follow-up RFC for smarter compression tiers. I can flip the param.

rachel: +1 on exact-percentile fallback for small-sample rollups. we already store raw histograms for 24h; could compute exact quantile on-demand.

mike: action items: owen flip compression back in prod, ux-lina mock sample_count/highlight unreliable badge, rachel draft fallback compute design, jess add dashboard threshold rules.

ux-lina: will post 2 mock variants: inline badge vs tooltip callout. the inline badge shows samples and method.

own: flipped compression back to 200 in prod at 7765434000. will monitor.

infra-bot: deploy: metrics-config v3.4 applied at 7765434000 (by owen).

mike: re-running checks now. initial glance looks closer to raw per-host p99. i'll report back in ~10m.

jess: long-term we should also surface the aggregation algorithm (t-digest vs histogram) and compression settings in the console so incident responders don't get surprised.

rachel: agree. I'll start a short postmortem note linking the autoscale tweak and outline the exact-percentile fallback.

mike: thanks everyone. small wins: chart legend needs a sample_count and an "estimation method" label. leaving this open until stable.
